name: Step Jack
description_en:
The Step Jack is a low-impact plyometric-style move that provides cardiovascular benefits without the joint stress of jumping. It works the entire body, specifically targeting the legs, core, and shoulders. This move is ideal for beginners, individuals with joint sensitivities, or as a dynamic warm-up to gradually elevate the heart rate.
Notes (Instructions):
​Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides.
​Step your right foot out to the side while simultaneously swinging both arms up above your head.
Bring your right foot back to the center and lower your arms.
​Immediately repeat the movement, stepping out with your left foot.
​Continue alternating sides at a steady, rhythmic pace.

name: Slow Squat
description_en:
​A tempo-based squat that uses controlled movement to increase muscle tension and improve lower-body stability.
​Lower: Descend slowly for 3 seconds.
​Pause: Hold at the bottom for 1 second.
​Stand: Return to the starting position at a normal pace.
Form: Keep your chest up and weight in your heels.

name: Wide Push-Up
description_en:
​A push-up variation with a wider hand placement to increase the emphasis on the outer chest muscles and shoulders.
​Setup: Place hands wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor.
Lower: Descend until your chest nearly touches the floor, keeping your core tight.
​Push: Drive through your palms to return to the start position.
​Form: Don't let your lower back sag; keep a straight line from head to heels.

name: Marching High Knees
description_en:
A low-impact cardio and mobility exercise that strengthens the hip flexors and improves balance.
​Movement: Stand tall and lift one knee toward your chest as high as comfortable.
​Arms: Swing the opposite arm forward as you lift your knee, similar to a walking motion.
​Core: Keep your abs engaged to maintain an upright posture.
​Pace: Perform the movement with control, alternating legs rhythmically.

name: 1/2 Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
description_en:
Begin in a half kneeling position with the
leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall
with a ball.
With both hands directly in front of
you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach
the wall behind you.
Exhale as you rotate, inhale
as you return to neutral and repeat.

name: Reverse Clamshell
description_en:
Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your knees stacked on top of each other. Keep your feet together at first, then keep your knees touching while lifting your top foot upward. Slowly lower the foot back down with control.
Move only through the hip and avoid rolling your pelvis backward. The movement should be small, controlled, and focused on hip rotation.

name: Clamshell to Reverse Clamshell
description_en:
Lie on your side with your hips and knees bent, keeping your legs stacked. Lift your top knee into a clamshell position and keep the leg elevated throughout the movement. From there, alternate between opening the knee upward and lifting the foot upward, moving through hip external and internal rotation.
Keep the movement slow and controlled. Do not let the top leg rest on the bottom leg between repetitions.

name: YTW Raises
description_en: The YTW exercise for scapular retraction is designed to strengthen the inter-scapular muscles between your shoulder blades, to help retract or pull your shoulders back, helping to maintain proper upright posture.

name: Posterior Pelvic Tilt
description_en: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Flatten your lower back against the floor by tilting your pelvis posteriorly, engaging your abs and glutes. Hold 5 seconds, release. This retrains pelvic positioning to counter anterior pelvic tilt.

name: explosive push ups
description_en:
Explosive Push-Ups
Start in a standard push-up position, lower your chest, then explosively push off the ground so your hands leave the floor. Land softly and immediately repeat.

name: Russian Push Ups
description_en:
Russian Push-Ups
Start in a standard push-up position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Lower your chest toward the floor, then shift your body forward while keeping your chest close to the ground. Extend your arms to return to the starting position, then reverse the movement smoothly. Keep your core tight and maintain controlled movement throughout the exercise.

name: elbow lever
description_en: ​A calisthenics static balance skill where the entire body is held straight and parallel to the ground, supported by tucking the elbows firmly into the abdomen or pelvic bones.

name: Planche Lean Hold
description_en: A straight-arm calisthenics static hold where you assume a plank position and lean the shoulders as far forward as possible past the wrists with protracted scapulae and a hollow body.

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
description_en:
Sit on the floor with one leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you and the other leg bent at 90 degrees out to the side, so that the rear shin is parallel to the front shin. Keep your torso upright and, if possible, your hands off the floor.
Rotate both knees over to the other side so that the legs swap positions and you arrive in the same 90/90 position facing the opposite way. Move slowly and under control, keeping the feet in contact with the floor, and alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
Mobility drill for internal and external rotation of the hips.

name: Adductor Rock Backs
description_en:
Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot flat on the floor and the toes pointing forward.
Keep your back flat and slowly push your hips back towards the heel of the kneeling leg until you feel a stretch along the inside of the extended leg. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position. Complete all repetitions on one side before switching legs.
Mobility exercise for the adductors and the hips.

name: Elevated Hamstring Stretch
description_en:
Stand facing a bar, box or bench at roughly hip height and place the heel of one leg on it. Keep that leg straight with the toes pointing up, and keep the standing leg straight with both hips square to the support.
Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until you feel a stretch in the back of the elevated thigh. Hold the position while breathing calmly, then switch legs.
Stretch for the hamstrings. The height of the support controls the intensity: the higher the leg, the stronger the stretch.

name: Single-leg BOSU balance
description_en:
Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
The exercise for balancing on a BOSU ball while standing on one leg is known as the single-leg BOSU balance exercise. This exercise is effective for enhancing balance, coordination, and core stability.
Benefits of the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
Improves Balance:
 Standing on one leg challenges your stability.
Enhances Coordination:
 Engaging different muscle groups helps improve overall coordination.
Strengthens Core:
 The exercise activates core muscles, promoting better posture and stability.
How to Perform the Single-Leg BOSU Balance Exercise
Positioning:
 Stand on the dome side of the BOSU ball with one leg.
Balance:
 Keep your opposite leg lifted and your core engaged.
Duration:
 Aim to hold the position for 10-20 seconds, gradually increasing the time as you improve.
Progression Tips
Add Movement:
 Try reaching for objects around you while maintaining balance.
Close Your Eyes:
 This increases the challenge by removing visual stability cues.
Use a Ball:
 Catch or toss a ball while balancing to further engage your core and coordination.
This exercise is a great way to build foundational balance skills before progressing to more complex movements.

name: Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
description_en:
Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
Single-leg soft-landing holds are exercises that focus on balance and stability by landing softly on one leg and holding the position. This exercise helps improve proprioception and can be beneficial for rehabilitation and athletic training.
Overview
Single-leg soft-landing holds are exercises designed to enhance balance, stability, and proprioception. They involve landing softly on one leg and maintaining that position for a brief period. This exercise is particularly useful in rehabilitation settings and for athletes looking to improve their performance.
Benefits
Improves balance:
 Enhances stability by training the body to control weight distribution on one leg.
Enhances proprioception:
 Increases awareness of body position, which is crucial for injury prevention.
Supports rehabilitation:
 Helps individuals recover from lower-limb injuries by strengthening muscles and improving joint stability.
How to Perform Single-Leg Soft-Landing Holds
Steps
Preparation:
 Stand on a stable surface or a box.
Takeoff:
 Step off the box or surface with one leg, ensuring that you do not jump.
Landing:
 Land softly on the target leg, allowing the knee and hip to bend slightly.
Hold position:
 Maintain balance in the landed position for up to 2 seconds.
Reset:
 Return to the starting position and repeat.
Key Points to Remember
Keep your chest up and engage your core for better stability.
Ensure your knee aligns with the midline of your foot during landing.
Focus on a controlled descent to minimize impact.
Conclusion
Incorporating single-leg soft-landing holds into your training routine can significantly enhance your balance and stability, making it a valuable exercise for both rehabilitation and athletic performance.

name: Box Handstand Push-up
description_en: Pike push-up with legs on an elevated surface. Progression to handstand push-up.

name: FlexBar Wrist Extension
description_en: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing down and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist drop, then extend the wrist to raise the bar, keeping the forearm still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. The resistance comes from twisting or bending the flexible bar, so a thicker or stiffer bar increases the load. Commonly used for wrist and forearm strengthening and for elbow tendon rehabilitation.

name: FlexBar Wrist Flexion
description_en: Performed with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar. Rest your forearm on your thigh or a table with the palm facing up and the wrist just past the edge. Hold the bar in that hand, let the wrist extend back, then curl the wrist up to raise the bar while the forearm stays still. Lower slowly, taking about three seconds. Works the wrist flexors, and is the companion movement to FlexBar wrist extension for balanced forearm strengthening.

name: FlexBar Tyler Twist
description_en: An eccentric exercise for the wrist extensors, done with a flexible resistance bar such as a Theraband FlexBar, and widely used in rehabilitation for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow). Hold the bar vertically in the affected hand with the wrist extended. Grasp the top of the bar with the other hand, palm facing away, and twist the top hand to wind up the bar. Bring both arms out in front of you with the bar horizontal, then slowly let the affected wrist untwist the bar over about four seconds while the other hand holds steady. Reset and repeat. The reverse version, twisting in the opposite direction for the wrist flexors, is used for medial epicondylitis (golfer's elbow). Move slowly and stop if the exercise causes sharp pain rather than the expected mild discomfort.

name: Seated Knee Extension with Overpressure
description_en: A gentle stretch to restore full knee extension. Sit with one leg stretched out in front of you and the heel propped on the floor or a low surface, so the knee is unsupported. Place both hands on the thigh just above the kneecap. Keeping the leg relaxed, gently press down through the hands toward the floor until you feel a stretch behind the knee, and hold for about three seconds before releasing. The pressure should produce a stretch, never sharp pain. Repeat for the prescribed number of repetitions, then switch legs.

name: Step Calf Stretch
description_en: Stand on a step or a sturdy raised surface with the balls of both feet on the edge and the heels hanging off, holding a rail or wall for balance. Let one or both heels drop below the level of the step until you feel a stretch through the calf, and hold. Keep the knee straight to stretch the gastrocnemius, or bend the knee slightly to bias the soleus lower down. Hold for the prescribed time, typically 30 seconds, without bouncing, then switch sides if stretching one leg at a time.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Eyes Closed
description_en: A balance and proprioception drill. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent and the other foot lifted clear of the floor, then close your eyes and hold the position. Without visual feedback the ankle and hip stabilisers have to do the work, so expect noticeable wobble. Stand within reach of a wall, counter or chair so you can steady yourself if needed. Hold for the prescribed time, then switch legs. Commonly prescribed in rehabilitation after ankle or knee injury.

name: Alternate Walking
description_en: 1m30s of walking (~4.5 km/h) to 30 s of jog (7 km/h) and repeat

name: Radio Taiso
description_en:
Video can be found here : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGPBSqxKGAc
Full-body mobility and dynamic warm-up routine (3–5 minutes) to prepare joints, muscles, and the cardiovascular system for workout.
Movement Flow:
Deep Breathing & Arm Raises: Inhale while raising arms laterally overhead, exhale as you lower them.
Knee Bends: Soft, rhythmic knee flexions synchronized with arm swings.
Arm Circles: Large full-range arm rotations forward, then backward to open up the chest and shoulder girdle.
Chest Expansion: Cross arms in front of the chest and open wide to the sides.
Side Bends: Reach overhead to stretch the lateral torso left and right with a smooth side flexion.
Forward & Back Bends: Gently hinge at the hips to reach forward, then return upright with a mild spinal extension.
Torso Twists: Swing arms side-to-side to rotate the spine and loosen the core.
Ankle Mobility / Light Bounces: Soft heel lifts or light bouncing on toes to warm up lower leg joints and tendons.

name: Stomach Vacuum
description_en:
Starting position
: Lie flat on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the floor (or stand/sit upright).
Exhalation
: Fully exhale all the air from your lungs through your mouth.
Contraction
: Draw your navel in towards your spine as far as possible, pulling your stomach inward and up under your ribcage.
Hold
: Hold this isometric contraction without breathing for 10 to 20 seconds.
Release
: Slowly inhale through your nose to release the tension and relax your abdominals.
Repeat
: Rest briefly and perform the desired number of sets.

name: Wrist rocks
description_en: Start on all fours with your palms flat on the floor. Slowly rock forward and backward, keeping your hands planted. Move only within a comfortable, pain-free wrist range to gently improve mobility and flexibility.

name: Scapular Pushups
description_en: Start in a straight-arm plank with your hands under your shoulders. Keep your elbows locked and move only your shoulder blades: let your chest sink slightly, then push the floor away to spread the shoulder blades. Move in a comfortable, controlled range.

name: Triceps push up
description_en:
Push ups for targeting triceps.
Start with a plank position with your hands directly below your shoulders, feet together.
When descending, keep your elbows pinned to your sides. Upper arms straight back.
Lower until your chest touches the floor, then return.

name: Cross-Body Stretch
description_en: Extend your right arm straight across your chest toward the left. Hook your left arm around your right elbow and pull your right arm a little closer to your body. Keep your shoulder down as you do this. Repeat on the other side.

name: Wrist Stretch
description_en: Extend your right arm straight out in front of you, with your palm facing up (fingers pointing toward the floor). Using your left hand, gently pull the fingers of your right hand toward you until you feel a stretch in your forearm and biceps.

name: Quadriceps Stretch
description_en: Stand on one leg (hold onto a wall if necessary). Use your hand to grasp the ankle of your other leg and gently pull your heel toward your buttocks. Make sure your knees stay close together and that you push your pelvis slightly forward (avoid arching your back).

name: Hamstring Stretch
description_en: Sit on the floor. Extend your right leg straight out in front of you. Bend your left leg and place the sole of your left foot against the inner side of your right thigh (with your knee pointing to the side). Straighten your upper body completely (chest out, shoulders back). Inhale, and as you exhale, bend forward from the hips (not the lower back!) over your extended right leg. Reach for your shin, ankle, or foot—whichever is possible while keeping your back straight.

name: V-Up - Mark Lauren
description_en:
One of the best exercises for the rectus abdominis muscles. Lie on your back with your legs straight and your arms close to your sides. Lift your head off the floor and raise your legs and arms about 15 centimeters off the floor. Your palms should face down, and look up at the ceiling.
Now bend your legs and at the same time sit up so that your knees and chest almost touch. Only your buttocks are still on the floor. Your arms are now extended at shoulder height. Then slowly return to the starting position with your arms and legs extended and your head raised.

name: Pike Hold (Floor)
description_en: A static bodyweight support with both hands and feet on the floor and hips raised in a pike position. Place your hands and feet securely on the floor, then raise your hips. Keep your elbows straight and actively push the floor away through your shoulders. Maintain a controlled, stationary position without bending your elbows, lowering your head for push-up repetitions, or raising your feet onto a surface. Hold for up to 30 seconds. Stop earlier for loss of alignment, loss of active shoulder support, or pain. Record actual seconds, hand and foot spacing, and alignment. This is the floor variation, not a pike push-up or an elevated-feet pike hold.

name: 2 Handed Kettlebell Swing
description_en: Two Handed Russian Style Kettlebell swing

name: Kettlebell Swings
description_en:
Hold the kettlebell securely in both hands. Keep your back flat throughout the move, avoiding any rounding of the spine.Keeping your knees "soft", hinge your hips backwards, letting the kettlebell swing between your knees.
You want to bend from the hips as far as you can 
without letting your back round forwards
. Then, snap your hips forwards quickly and standing up straight, locking your body in an upright posture.
The speed you do this will cause your arms and the kettlebell to swing up in front of you. Don't try to 
lift
 the kettlebell with your arms. The snapping forwards of your hips will cause the kettlebell to swing forwards through momentum. Depending on the weight of the kettlebell and the speed of your hip movement, your arms will swing up to about shoulder height. At the top of this swing, let your hips hinge backwards again as the kettlebell swings back down to between your legs and the start of the next repetition.

name: Kettlebell Swing
description_en: While kettlebell swings are a full-body workout, they mostly target the muscles along the posterior chain (back of the body). The main muscles used are the glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, and muscles of the upper back.

name: Curl with kettlebell two hands
description_en: Stand upright and grip the kettlebell with both hands. Perform the elbow flexion motion, starting from a fully extended position until your hand reaches shoulder height. Spread your legs a little for stability and, to perform the exercise correctly, try not to push with your back or body in general. Change the weight of the kettlebell to adjust the difficulty.

name: one-handed kettlebell curls
description_en: Standing with the kettlebell in one hand and bent at the elbow, start from a fully extended position until your hand reaches shoulder height. To perform the movement correctly, try not to push with your back or body.

name: Kettlebell deadlifts
description_en:
Starting position:
Stand hip-width apart, with your kettlebell centered between your ankles. Your back should be straight, your head facing forward.
Steps:
Hinge at the hips and slightly bend at the knees to put your hands on the kettlebell handles. Your back should be straight as you perform the movement.
Grab the kettlebell handles, with your hands pushing in opposite directions as if to pull the handle apart.
While contacting your abs and glutes, stand straight up.
Hinge at the hips again to bring the kettlebell back down, similarly to step 1.
Repeat from step 3.
Tips:
Be sure you're performing the movements correctly, as doing otherwise can lead to injury. For example, do not squat instead of hinging at the hips, do not round your back while reaching for the kettlebell, and do not lean back while standing up.

name: Single Arm Plank to Row
description_en: Start position as row, extend to plank and back. Finish with row and repeat

name: Dynamic side hold
description_en: Sling a rubber band on a kettlebell and lift the kettlebell by the rubber band. Let it hang by your side and stand on one leg, switch leg while continuing hold. Repeat with other hand

name: Double Kettlebell Clean and Press
description_en: Full-body muscles building exercise. This exercise provides a huge range of benefits in terms of strength & size and is extremely functional.

name: Double Kettlebell Front Squat
description_en: The kettlebell front squat is a compound, multi-joint exercise that works several muscle groups.

name: kettlebell sumo deadlift
description_en:
Place your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, pointing your toes outward.
Keep your back straight, shoulders back, and chest up.
The knees must follow the same direction as the toes and not move forward.
When going up, it is advisable to contract your glutes to maximize the effectiveness of the exercise..

name: Blaze
description_en: BLAZE is a full-body HIIT workout. Designed to supercharge your cardio fitness and strength. Delivered in its own purpose-built studio, BLAZE is a unique mix of martial arts, intense cardio and strength training.

name: Kettlebell One Legged Deadlift
description_en: This exercise involves holding a kettlebell in one hand and standing on one leg while bending forward to touch the kettlebell to the ground. It targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back while also improving balance and stability.

name: Single-Leg Lunge with Kettlebell:
description_en:
How to do a single-leg kettlebell lunge
Preparation: Stand with your feet together. Hold the kettlebell with both hands by the handle, keeping it close to your chest, or hold it with one hand (on the same side as the working leg).
Step and Lower: Take a large step forward (or backward, which is safer for your knees) with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees form a 90-degree angle.
Focus: Shift your weight onto your front (or bent) leg, keeping your back straight and your torso upright.
Return: Push off with your front leg to return to the starting position.

name: Kettlebell sumo high pull
description_en:
A compound exercise combining elements of a sumo deadlift and a high pull. It targets the posterior chain, particularly the glutes, hamstrings, and upper back. The sumo stance increases hip engagement, while the high pull adds an explosive element, promoting power development.
Stand upright overtop of a kettlebell with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart angled out slightly.
Maintain a braced core and neutral spine throughout the exercise.
Hinge your hips backward and extend your arms to grab ahold the kettlebell with a double overhand grip.
With you lower legs nearly vertical to the ground, extend your hips to raise the kettlebell with your elbows high keeping it close to your body.
Once the kettlebell has reached shoulder height, lower back to the starting position.

name: Hip Airplane
description_en:
Stand on one leg and lean your upper body slightly forward while keeping your back straight. Extend the free leg behind you so that your torso and leg form roughly one line. Slowly open your hip to the side by rotating your pelvis and upper body in a controlled way. Then close the hip again and return to the starting position.
The movement should mainly come from the hip. Keep your standing foot stable and avoid letting your knee collapse inward.

name: Single-Leg Balance with Kettlebell Circles
description_en: A balance drill that adds a moving load. Stand on one leg with the knee slightly bent, holding a kettlebell in one hand. Pass the kettlebell around your body in a circle, handing it from one hand to the other in front and behind you, while keeping your balance on the standing leg. Keep the hips level and the torso upright; the shifting weight of the bell constantly changes your centre of mass, which is what trains the hip and ankle stabilisers. Complete the prescribed number of circles, reverse direction, then switch legs. Use a light bell to start.
